title: Wartime intelligence agencies run by financiers

tellings.quote: People don't know, there was also another American intelligence agency dedicated to South America, which is the Office for the Coordination of Inter-American Affairs.

plain: During the Second World War, besides the better-known American spy agency, there was another US intelligence agency devoted to South America, the Office for the Coordination of Inter-American Affairs, according to the researcher Jason Simosa. He tells Jesse Michels this from his own research, naming figures such as William Donovan, Allen Dulles, Nelson Rockefeller, William Stephenson and Charles Hambro, and argues that wartime intelligence in the US and Britain was run largely by financiers. He raises it to suggest that private wealth and state secrecy have long been tangled together.
